title: VoteMate launches an AI assistant for ballot research
summary: VoteMate provides conversational ballot research, while improvements in voter knowledge and participation remain unmeasured in the reviewed sources.
account: VoteMate announced the nationwide launch of its free AI ballot assistant on October 16, 2025. Its original release described conversational, multilingual access to candidate and ballot-measure information and reported that the soft launch had reached thousands of voters in 30 states. In May 2026, Ballotpedia confirmed an agreement for direct integration of its election data. VoteMate’s October 2026 transparency page describes several model providers, human review of AI-written candidate profiles, and connections to official and civic data sources. These publications establish the service and its intended accessibility benefits, but do not measure changes in voter knowledge, accuracy, participation, or turnout. The AI Opportunity Inventory submission reports 7,652 beta users and acknowledges the absence of measured effects on voters. That usage count is not a benefit estimate.
purpose: Help voters research candidates, measures, and voting information through a conversational interface.

ratings.reason: The reviewed material does not establish a scoped benefit magnitude for this stakeholder group.

ai_role.statement: Language models organize election information and answer questions using retrieved sources. A voter-benefit comparison has not been established. The October 2026 provider list does not establish the model used throughout the 2025 beta.
